summary: Intermittent 5xx spike from prefetch-circuit coupling causing memory pressure and runtime restart loop
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ChorusAI) reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses on streaming and short-request routes starting 2026-03-13 14:10 UTC. Errors manifest as 502/503 from API gateway, and upstream runtimes in the customers dedicated pool repeatedly restart. Impact: customer reports degraded UX (failed chat completions) and elevated token-level retries.

Impact:
- ~35% error rate on the affected route for the tenant during the peak window.
- Multiple upstream runtime processes observed OOM/restarts.
- Customer requests are predominantly small/prefix-heavy (streaming chat) mixed with a small embedding upload job.

Environment:
- Dedicated tenant cluster in us-east-1, production.
- Autoscaler: dedicated-gpu-pool-v3.

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1. Tenant performs a short burst of streaming chat traffic (100-200 RPS) concurrently with a 50k-row embedding upload pipeline.
2. API gateway begins shedding/hedging requests; some requests placed in prefetch queue.
3. Prefetch circuit engages (queue backpressure + cancellation), then a wave of downstream runtime OOMs and restarts occurs, followed by API gateway 502/503 responses.

Observed at: 2026-03-13 14:10 UTC onward.
steps_to_reproduce: See description; reproduction is traffic-mix dependent (streaming + embedding upload). Not reliably reproducible in staging without the same mixed payload profile.
logs_and_metrics:
Key signals:
- apigw/error_rate (tenant route): spike from 0.5% -> 35% at 14:12 UTC.
- runtime/oom_events (dedicated pool): 18 OOMs between 14:12-14:28 UTC.
- kv-cache/lock-wait-ms: long tail increase concurrent with prefetch cancellations.
- system/mem_pressure: host RSS growing prior to crash; swap activity minimal.
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/tenant-errors, https://kibana.redwood.internal/tenant-logs?query=SUP-386007
Relevant logs: runtime stderr shows repeated "Failed to allocate contiguous buffer for KV cache" and watchdog restarts with exit_code 137.
investigation_notes: 14:25 UTC: Initial triage by Support (Maria). Pattern shows prefetch cancellations correlate strongly with runtime OOM bursts.
14:45 UTC: SRE (Ethan) confirmed sustained high mem RSS on two GPU hosts prior to container SIGKILL. NVML logs show no GPU OOMs; host memory exhaustion appears likely.

15:10 UTC: Noted embedding upload pipeline opens many short-lived connections that trigger aggressive prefetch entries; prefetcher holds locks during cancellation and dealloc path leads to temporary memory spike in runtime process.

15:30 UTC: Hypothesis: coupling between prefetch circuit, lock contention in kv-cache, and allocator fragmentation causing transient host memory pressure that leads to runtime watchdog kills and a 5xx wave from API gateway.
15:55 UTC: Correlated with an autoscaler warmup phase that had several ephemeral workers starting; these workers increased overall memory fragmentation on hosts with mixed tenant workloads.
comments: 2026-03-13 14:30 UTC - Maria Gonzalez: Customer: "We see repeated 502s, chat sessions drop mid-stream. Started after an embedding migration job." Customer provided request ids: r_0a1bf..r_0a1c9. Asked for logs and recent deploys.

2026-03-13 14:50 UTC - Ethan Park (SRE): Captured host-level dmesg and container OOM logs; no GPU resets. Suspect host RAM fragmentation + allocator path. Spun up extra diagnostic agents on the dedicated pool.

2026-03-13 15:20 UTC - Support Engineer (Liam Chen): Applied a temporary rate cap on the tenant's bulk embedding uploads to reduce concurrent prefetch entries. Observed error rate drop from 35% -> 8% over 10 minutes.
2026-03-13 16:05 UTC - Maria Gonzalez: Customer confirmed UX improved after rate cap. Asked for root cause and permanent mitigation plan.

2026-03-13 17:00 UTC - Ethan Park: Scheduled follow-up with runtime team to add guard rails in prefetcher deallocation code path and review allocator behavior under many cancellations. See PR drafts in linked_github_prs.
root_cause_hypothesis: Prefetch circuit cancellation + KV-cache lock holding created allocation churn and fragmentation in runtime process memory allocator on hosts running mixed ephemeral workers; sustained allocation failures precipitated SIGKILLs by the runtime watchdog (OOM-like), producing upstream 5xx from API gateway.
workaround: Applied temporary ingestion rate limit on customer bulk embedding pipeline and reduced prefetch window for the tenant. This reduced lock contention and stopped the OOM cascade.
resolution_notes:
Work in progress: runtime team to harden prefetch deallocation path and add a defensive BPF-level oom-protection metric ingestion to avoid wholesale watchdog evictions. Plan: patch prefetcher to avoid long-held locks on cancel, release candidate rollouts in canary, monitor error-rate for 48h.
Temporary fix enacted: customer embedding rate throttled and prefetch window reduced (both reversible).
next_steps: 1) Runtime team to land PR to avoid allocator fragmentation (target: 2026-03-18). 2) Add telemetry to detect prefetch-cancel mem spikes. 3) Recommend product limit: soft rate cap on concurrent bulk uploads per tenant to avoid mixed workload coupling. 4) Postmortem and customer comms draft (owner: Maria).
customer_communication: 2026-03-13 18:30 UTC: Support notified customer of temporary mitigation and ongoing engineering work. Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix; provided target patch date 2026-03-18.
follow_up_items: Postmortem writeup and RCA (owner: Maria) due 2026-03-20
Instrumentation PR for prefetch telemetry (owner: Ethan) due 2026-03-16
